model: Regulated-utility dividend discount at cost of equity with exit multiple (engine route; rate-base compounding, net debt zero)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management's long-term adjusted EPS algorithm of 6-8%+ through 2030 (lower end taken), corroborated by the 5-year basic EPS CAGR of 6.4% (FY2020 $2.72 -> FY2025 $3.71) and the 5-year DPS CAGR of 5.6% ($2.05 -> $2.6975 declared).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book) CAGR of 3.3% diverges >30% from the EPS CAGR of 6.4%. Expected for a regulated utility: book equity is depressed by the $2.67B of 2018-2019 post-merger buybacks and a ~65% payout, while per-share earnings compound on RATE BASE (which grew ~8-9%/yr) and allowed ROE. The per-share EPS path, not book-value growth, is the right driver here; equity CAGR is not used.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue (FY2020 $4,913M -> FY2025 $5,962M) understates the economics because fuel and purchased power are pass-throughs and the FY2021 Winter Storm Uri spike inflates the 5-year base. FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is negative in every year FY2021-FY2025 (capex 1.1-1.4x OCF by design), so a CAGR is undefined and SBC-adjusting it changes nothing material (SBC $15-21M/yr). Equity-award taxes are not separately disclosed and are immaterial at this SBC scale.

scenario_narratives.base: Evergy delivers management's algorithm but not the beat: the raised FY2026 guide is treated as the weather-flattered year it is described as, FY2027 is a near-flat 'reset' year, then the $21.6B capital plan (12% rate base CAGR, $9.3B of new gas generation, LLPS-contracted data-centre load) drives 7-7.5% EPS growth 2028-2030. Dividends grow ~4%/yr toward a 57% payout. Discounted at a 7.75% cost of equity with a 3.5% terminal growth, the base case prices the stock at roughly 14x year-10 earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-centre thesis compounds: signed large-load agreements climb toward the 5-7 GW ambition, Missouri rate cases are constructive, CWIP recovery under SB4 removes regulatory lag, and the EPS algorithm is rebased off the higher 2026 base. EPS compounds 8.5-9% through 2030.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulation and dilution bite together: adverse Missouri orders, weather normalisation, heavier-than-planned convert and ATM dilution, and slipping hyperscaler timelines leave EPS growth at 4-5% while the capital plan is funded anyway. Still a solvent, dividend-paying utility -- the downside is a lower growth rate and a lower multiple, not impairment.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a compounder of rate base at an allowed ROE funded by retained earnings, debt and new equity; the only cash an outside shareholder receives is the dividend, so the model discounts dividends per share at the cost of equity with net debt at zero, and lets the terminal value be the lower of Gordon growth and a 28x dividend (~16x earnings) cap. Reported FCF is ignored as a valuation input because it is negative by design during a capital supercycle. The main judgement is the per-share EPS path -- whether the 2026 beat is a new base (bull) or a weather year (base/bear) -- and the result should be read as the price at which a 7.75% equity return is earned, with the 15% hurdle entry price far below it as it is for every low-growth bond-proxy.
key_risks_to_valuation: Missouri rate-case outcomes (Evergy Metro ~$140M ask at 10.5% ROE, order due by year-end 2026; Evergy Missouri West ~$229.5M ask at 10.25%, rates Oct-2027) set the 2027-2028 earnings base.
Large-load materialisation: 2.6-3.1 GW signed against a 5-7 GW target; the $9.3B new-generation build is sized for the pipeline.

Dilution: $1,155.9M 4.50% converts (in the money, convertible now, maturing Dec-2027), ~$0.5B of ATM capacity plus 4.7M shares under forward sales, ~$3.3B equity planned 2026-2030; per-share growth below the rate-base growth by ~250bp is the historical relationship management cites.
Interest rates: a 100bp move in the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 20-25% (see sensitivity grid); the 10-year UST at 4.86% is the anchor.
Weather: ~one-third of retail revenue books in Q3; the FY2026 raise was largely weather-driven by management's own account.
Coal fleet (~37% of capacity) and CCR/environmental rules: stranded-cost recovery not guaranteed outside IRP timing.
Nuclear PTC: IRS gross-receipts guidance in 2026 could cut the credit; any benefit is returned to customers, so it is a cash-flow timing item, not earnings.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 71.41-89.66. 10-year UST from Yahoo ^TNX the same day.
data_sources.financials: research/EVRG/Reports/EVRG_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts, FY2016-Q1 2026) for history; EVRG_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q text, extracted 2026-11-08) for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, 2026-10-30 share count, convert and ATM forward terms, Q3/9M adjusted EPS and the Oct-2026 dividend; EVRG_Annual_FY2025.txt for FY2025 adjusted EPS, dividends declared, the 2026-2030 capex table (:10410-10418) and dilutive securities (:11677-11690). FY2026 EPS guidance and the long-term algorithm from the Q3-2026 earnings release as summarised in EVRG_Analysis.json.
data_sources.qualitative: research/EVRG/Reports/EVRG_Analysis.json (2026-11-08); kpis table for allowed ROEs, customer counts and GWh sales.

inputs.base_revenue_note: ENGINE MAPPING: the 'revenue' slot carries ADJUSTED EARNINGS TO COMMON for FY2026E = guidance midpoint $4.425 x 241.0M fully diluted shares = $1,066M. Guidance $4.35-$4.50 raised Nov-2026 from $4.14-$4.34 (Q3-2026 10-Q :7346-7347: 9M-2026 adjusted EPS $4.15 vs $3.41; FY2025 adjusted $3.83, GAAP diluted $3.66, 10-K :10068).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the current price: 234.5M basic at 2026-10-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover :4888) + ~5.4M if-converted excess shares on the $1,155.9M 4.50% Convertible Notes due Dec-2027 (4.8M dilutive in Q3-2026 at the quarter's lower average price, :6038-6040; the sales-price condition is met and the notes are convertible through Dec-2026, :6590) + ~0.6M treasury-stock-method shares on the outstanding ATM forward sale agreements (4.7M shares vs $363.5M cash, :7214-7218) + ~1.2M RSUs/DSUs (10-K :14681). Held FLAT in the engine because growth_rates are PER-SHARE EPS growth (management's 6-8%+ algorithm is per share and already nets the ~$3.3B 2026-2030 ATM/forward equity programme); per-share values do not depend on this count, only the headline equity total does.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by construction: the discounted stream (dividends) is post-interest, so debt is already serviced inside earnings; deducting it again would double-count (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never FCF / WACC on a post-interest flow). Debt and cash below are recorded for audit only.
inputs.total_debt_note: 2026-09-30: current maturities of long-term debt $1,495.3M (includes the $1,155.9M converts, reclassified current) + long-term debt net $13,551.3M (Q3-2026 10-Q :5173, :5185). Excludes commercial paper. Year-end 2025 was $13,406.2M.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E dividends declared to common = $2.8075/share (0.6950 x 3 + 0.7225 declared Oct-2026, Q3-2026 10-Q :5373-5392, :6091) x 241.0M = $676.6M. This is the FY0 flow the engine compounds. Reported owner FCF is NOT the stream (see reported_fcf).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF = OCF $2,045.2M - capex $2,796.9M = -$751.7M (Metrics CSV). 9M-2026: OCF $1,699.2M - additions $2,714.6M = -$1,015M (Q3-2026 10-Q :5292-5294). Structurally negative through the $21.6B 2026-2030 capital plan; that capex enters rate base and earns an allowed 9.4-9.7% ROE, so an unlevered owner-FCF DCF would value the equity at ~nothing -- a method artefact (AIA.NZ, AEE, ETR, AEP precedents), not a finding.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement 'Stock compensation' $20.7M (Metrics CSV StockBasedComp); 9M-2026 $19.2M (Q3-2026 10-Q :5273). SBC is 0.35% of revenue and is already EXPENSED inside GAAP and adjusted earnings (Evergy's adjusted EPS does not add it back), so sbc_pct_path is 0 and house = street.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases since FY2019 ($1,628.7M in FY2019, $1,042.3M in FY2018, kpis.buybacks). Evergy is a net ISSUER: ~3.9M shares for $321.2M via the ATM in Sep-2026 (:7203-7205) and ~$3.3B planned 2026-2030. The dilution is netted inside the per-share growth path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is the COST OF EQUITY (7.75%), because the stream is dividends out of post-interest earnings. USD build: 10-year UST 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX close 2026-11-06) + regulated-utility equity beta ~0.55 x ERP 5.0-5.5% = 7.6-7.9%; 7.75% taken -- a quarter-point above Ameren (7.5%, the closest Midwest/Missouri peer) for the BBB+ holdco leverage, the live convert dilution and a capital plan equal to its entire 2025 rate base, and below AEP/Eversource (8.0%). Identical across the three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the paths and weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Cross-check: allowed ROEs are 9.4% (Metro Kansas), 9.7% (Kansas Central) and 10.25-10.5% requested in Missouri; the market pays ~1.9x book and ~19.8x FY2026E adjusted EPS, consistent with a market cost of equity near 7.5-8%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial ($2.3-2.7M annual lease interest, 10-K :14386) and inside O&M, hence inside earnings.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial (<$1M). Earnings used are attributable to Evergy, Inc.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Evergy is a rate-regulated electric utility (Kansas/Missouri, single segment): earnings = allowed ROE x the equity layer of rate base, and growth comes from capex that regulators admit to rate base (~$20.7B 2025 -> ~$36B 2030, ~12% CAGR). dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no utility row; the operating-company row (owner-FCF DCF) is wrong here because reported FCF is structurally negative by design (FY2021-FY2025: -621/-365/-354/-353/-752; 9M-2026 -1,015) while the capex that drives it earns a regulated return above the cost of capital -- the firm-level DCF would be >100% terminal value against $15B of debt and return negative equity for a company earning ~9% on book. Per the skill's principle ('discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues') and the folder precedent for regulated utilities (ES, AEP, ETR, AEE; GPT.AX/GMG.AX for the engine pattern), the model is a DIVIDEND DISCOUNT at cost of equity run through the engine: revenue slot = adjusted earnings to common; growth_rates = per-share adjusted EPS growth (nets planned equity issuance and convert dilution); ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio, so engine FCF = dividends to common; sbc/D&A/capex/tax paths = 0 (all inside earnings); wc_capture 0; net_debt 0; terminal = min(Gordon on year-10 dividends at CoE, 28x year-10 dividends). Dividends, not earnings, are the stream because the ~40% retained is what funds the growth already in the EPS path; capitalising earnings would count it twice. CROSS-CHECK: the base-case terminal Gordon multiple (1.035/0.0425 = 24.4x dividends at a 57% payout) implies a ~13.9x exit P/E on year-10 EPS, well below the sector's ~17-19x forward; the valuation is deliberately not assuming today's multiple persists. FY0 is FY2026E (guidance midpoint), so Y1 = FY2027. SEC XBRL has not indexed the Q2/Q3-2026 10-Qs (a SEC-side gap as of 2026-11-08); the Q3-2026 10-Q TEXT is extracted and was used for every anchor above.

bear.narrative: FY2027 EPS falls 3% as normal weather reverses the 2026 windfall, the MPSC trims the Metro and Missouri West asks (ROE below 9.5%, lower equity ratio), and the $1.16B converts plus ATM forwards dilute faster than rate base converts to earnings. Large-load projects slip or scale back, leaving the $21.6B plan partly overbuilt; growth runs 4-5% through 2030 (FY2030 EPS ~$4.92, a 3.8% CAGR off $4.24) and fades to 3%. The dividend is held, so payout peaks at 68% before easing to 60%; terminal growth 3.0%.

base.narrative: FY2027 EPS grows only 2.5% off the raised FY2026E midpoint ($4.425 -> ~$4.54), because management holds the 6-8% algorithm to the ORIGINAL $4.24 midpoint and frames the 2026 beat as weather; 2028-2030 run 7-7.5% (a haircut to management's '>8%' for Missouri rate-case lag and ATM/convert dilution), landing FY2030 EPS at ~$5.61, the 7% midpoint path off $4.24. Growth then fades to 3.5% by year 10 as the 2026-2030 generation build rolls off. Payout drifts from 64% to 57% as the dividend grows ~4%/yr against 7% EPS, inside the 50-60% target range by 2030.

bull.narrative: The 2026 step-up proves durable (weather-normalised large-load demand, not weather): the algorithm is effectively rebased off $4.425, FY2027 +6%, then 8.5-9% through 2030 as the 5-7 GW pipeline fills beyond the 2.6-3.1 GW signed, Missouri grants the Metro and Missouri West asks near the 10.25-10.5% requested ROE, and SB4 CWIP recovery removes lag on the CCGT build. FY2030 EPS ~$6.05. Faster EPS lets the payout settle at 56%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 28x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear is lifted to 25% because the thesis sits on two binary regulatory outcomes (Evergy Metro order due by year-end 2026, Missouri West in 2027), the 2026 beat is self-described as weather, and dilution from the in-the-money converts and ATM forwards is certain while the large-load revenue is only ~half contracted. Bull is cut to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once (pipeline fill, constructive Missouri ROEs, on-time CCGT construction with a single-vendor power island). No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear is not pushed higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
